AI\D NOW, this 28th day of January 2026, the Delaware Public Service Commission
("Commission") determines and orders the following:
WHEREAS, on August 17,2017, Delmarva Power and Light Company (Delmarva" or
the "Company") filed an application ("Docket 17-0977") for an increase in elecffic distribution
rates; and
WHEREAS, on August 21., 20t8, the Delaware Public Service Commission (the
"Commission") adopted Order No. 9248 in Docket No. 17-0977, which approved a settlement
agreement (the "Sefflement Agreement") entered into by all parties in Docket 17-0977: and
WHEREAS, Section II.1.(c) of the Settlement Agreement addressed the impact of the Tax
Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017 (TCJA") and the process for how the Company's Excess Deferred
Income Taxes ("EDIT") would be flowed back to customers; specifically, $44-3 million of non-
protected property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a six-year amortization period, and
520.8 million of non-protected non-property related EDIT was to be flowed back using a five-year
amortization period; I and
' $62.5 million and $29.3 million respectively when grossed up by the revenue conversion factor of 1.40926

PSC DocketNo. 17-0977,Order No. 10941 Cont'd
WHEREAS, on November 24,2025,Delmarva filed an application (the "Application") to
modifu its electric Rider "EDIT" Excess Deferred Income Tax Credit ("Rider EDIT"); and
WHEREAS, Delmarva intends to reset to zero ($0.000000) certain Rider EDIT service
classifications whose EDIT liability balances have been fully credited to the respective customers;
and
WHEREAS, pursuant to Section II.1.(c)(vii) of the Settlement Agreement, because the
amounts due to the customers in each service classification could not be calculated precisely at the
time of the Settlement Agreement, the parties agreed that any amounts paid to customers in excess
of the total EDIT balance will be recorded as a regulatory asset with a retum at the Company's
Commission authorized rate of return to be recovered in the Company's subsequent rate case; and
WHEREAS, Delmarva has requested similar treatment to that received in PSC Order No.
10135, issued December 14,2022, PSC Order No. 10179, issued February 22,2023, PSC Order
No. 10282, issued August 23,2023, PSC Order No. 10338, issued November 29,2023, and PSC
Order No. 10518, issued August 21, 2024, that instead of carrying a regulatory asset balance for
the five-year EDIT credits, any regulatory asset balance be transferred to the respective six-year
regulatory liability balance to reduce the remaining liability if that balance still has a credit; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Medium General Service - Secondary
("MGS-S") six-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
January 2026. The Company intends to set the six-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective February 1,2026; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule I of the Application, the General Service - Primary ("GS-P")
six-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of January 2026.
2

PSC Docket No. 17-0977, Order No. 10941 Cont'd
The Company intends to set the six-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero effective February
1,2026; and
WHEREAS, per Schedule 1 of the Application, the Large General Service - Secondary
("LGS-S") five-year EDIT balance is estimated to be fully credited to the rate class by end of
January 2026. The Company intends to set the five-year EDIT credit for this rate class to zero
effective February 1,2026; and
WHEREAS, the Company requests authority to transfer any regulatory asset balance for
the LGS-S five-year EDIT credit to the respective six-year EDIT liability balance, thus reducing
the respective six-year EDIT liability balance; and
WHEREAS, Staff submitted a memorandum to the Commission recommending that 1)
the five-year EDIT credit for the LGS-S rate class be set to zero effective February I,2026, and
that any regulatory asset balance for this rate class be transferred to the respective six-year EDIT
liability balance; and2) the six-year EDIT credits for the MGS-S and GS-P rate classes be set to
zero effective February l, 2026, and any regulatory asset balances for these rate classes be
addressed in the Company's next rate case
NOW, THEREFORE,IT IS HEREBY ORDERED BY THE AFFIRMATIVE
VOTE OF NOT FEWER THAN THREB COMMISSIONERS:
That the six-year EDIT credits for the MGS-S and GS-P rate classes be set to zero
($0.000000) effective February l, 2026.
That any regulatory asset balances resulting from the six-year EDIT credit for the
MGS-S and GS-P rate classes will be addressed in Delmarva's next rate case.
That the five-year EDIT credit for the LGS-S rate class be set to zero ($0.000000)
effective February l, 2026.
